s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
Lesions range from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
key_facts: 2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions are round, hypopigmented macules
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions have gradually coalesced
No hair growth at the site of the lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Stroma is formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis is observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Nevus sebaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells, consistent with nevus sebaceus

shortlist.label: Syringoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multiple round, hypopigmented macules and histopathologic findings of neoplastic cords with glycogen accumulation, which can be seen in syringoma

shortlist.label: Trichoepithelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth, which can be features of trichoepithelioma

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck, consistent with idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of hypopigmented macules with sharp borders and absence of hair growth, which can be features of nevus depigmentosus
